points.title: 童年成长
points.description: 张爱玲出生于上海一个显赫的官宦世家，祖父张佩纶是清末名臣，外祖父李鸿章是洋务派领袖。她自幼接受中西合璧的教育，家庭环境优越但父母关系不和，母亲黄逸梵是一位新女性，与父亲张志沂离异后，张爱玲与弟弟跟随父亲生活。这段经历使她早早接触到人性的复杂与家庭关系的微妙，为她后来的文学创作提供了丰富素材。她在上海圣玛利亚女校接受教育，展现出非凡的文学天赋。
points.descriptionEn: Born in Shanghai to an illustrious official family, Eileen Chang's grandfather was the famous official Zhang Peilun, and her maternal grandfather was Li Hongzhang, a leader of the Self-Strengthening Movement. She received a blended Chinese and Western education in an affluent but troubled family. Her mother, Huang Yifu, was a modern woman who divorced her father, Zhang Zhiyi. After the divorce, Eileen and her younger brother lived with their father. This experience exposed her early to the complexities of human nature and family relationships, providing rich material for her later literary works. She studied at St. Mary's Hall for Girls in Shanghai, where she demonstrated extraordinary literary talent.

points.title: 求学时期
points.description: 张爱玲考入香港大学文科，主修英国文学。在香港的三年间，她广泛阅读西方文学作品，深受西方现代主义文学影响。这段时期她创作了《第一炉香》、《第二炉香》等早期作品，展现出独特的文学才华。1941年日军占领香港，张爱玲被迫中断学业返回上海，这段经历也使她对战争与人性有了更深刻的认识，为她后来的创作提供了新的视角。
points.descriptionEn: Eileen Chang enrolled in the University of Hong Kong, majoring in English literature. During her three years in Hong Kong, she extensively read Western literary works and was deeply influenced by Western modernist literature. During this period, she wrote early works such as 'The First Incense' and 'The Second Incense,' showcasing her unique literary talent. In 1941, when Japanese forces occupied Hong Kong, Eileen was forced to interrupt her studies and return to Shanghai. This experience gave her a deeper understanding of war and human nature, providing a new perspective for her later writing.

points.title: 文学生涯巅峰
points.description: 回到上海后，张爱玲迎来了她文学创作的黄金时期。她开始在《紫罗兰》、《杂志》等刊物上发表作品，包括《倾城之恋》、《金锁记》、《红玫瑰与白玫瑰》等经典小说。这些作品以细腻的心理描写、独特的女性视角和对都市生活的深刻洞察而著称。她与胡兰成的恋情也成为当时文坛的热门话题。这一时期，张爱玲确立了她在上海文坛的重要地位，成为中国现代文学史上最具影响力的女作家之一。
points.descriptionEn: After returning to Shanghai, Eileen Chang entered the golden period of her literary career. She began publishing works in magazines such as 'Violet' and 'Magazine,' including classic novels like 'Love in a Fallen City,' 'The Golden Cangue,' and 'Red Rose and White Rose.' These works were known for their delicate psychological descriptions, unique female perspective, and profound insights into urban life. Her romance with Hu Lancheng also became a hot topic in literary circles. During this period, Eileen established her important position in Shanghai's literary scene, becoming one of the most influential female writers in the history of modern Chinese literature.

points.title: 战后创作
points.description: 抗日战争胜利后，张爱玲继续在上海创作，发表了《十八春》、《半生缘》等作品。1947年，她与胡兰成离婚，结束了这段充满争议的感情。1949年新中国成立后，张爱玲选择留在上海，但她的作品逐渐受到政治环境的限制。这一时期，她开始创作英文作品，试图将自己的文学影响力扩展到国际舞台，包括《秧歌》、《赤地之恋》等作品，但反响平平。
points.descriptionEn: After the victory of the Anti-Japanese War, Eileen continued to create in Shanghai, publishing works such as 'Eighteen Springs' and 'Half a Lifetime of Fate.' In 1947, she divorced Hu Lancheng, ending this controversial relationship. After the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949, Eileen chose to remain in Shanghai, but her works gradually faced restrictions due to the political environment. During this period, she began writing in English, attempting to expand her literary influence to the international stage with works like 'The Rice-Sprout Song' and 'Naked Earth,' but received little response.

points.title: 香港过渡期
points.description: 1952年，张爱玲离开大陆前往香港，在美新处从事翻译工作。这一时期，她创作了《秧歌》、《赤地之恋》等英文小说，并尝试将中文作品翻译成英文。她在香港的生活相对平静，但文学创作不如在上海时期活跃。1954年，她与美国作家马宽德（Reyner Heppenstall）有过一段短暂的感情，但最终无果。香港时期是张爱玲人生的一个重要转折点，她开始为移居美国做准备。
points.descriptionEn: In 1952, Eileen left mainland China for Hong Kong, working as a translator for the United States Information Service. During this period, she wrote English novels such as 'The Rice-Sprout Song' and 'Naked Earth,' and attempted to translate her Chinese works into English. Her life in Hong Kong was relatively calm, but her literary activity was not as vibrant as in Shanghai. In 1954, she had a brief romance with American writer Reyner Heppenstall, but it ultimately came to nothing. The Hong Kong period was an important turning point in Eileen's life, as she began preparing to move to the United States.

points.title: 晚年生活
points.description: 1955年，张爱玲移居美国，在加州大学伯克利分校从事中国文学研究工作。1960年代，她与美国剧作家赖雅（Ferdinand Reyher）结婚，但这段婚姻也因赖雅的健康问题和经济困境而充满挑战。晚年，张爱玲逐渐淡出公众视野，过着隐居生活，专注于学术研究和文学创作。她完成了《红楼梦魇》等学术著作，并继续创作短篇小说。1995年9月，张爱玲在洛杉矶的公寓中孤独去世，数天后才被发现。她的晚年生活虽然清贫，但保持了独立的精神世界，对中国现代文学产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1955, Eileen Chang moved to the United States, working on Chinese literature research at the University of California, Berkeley. In the 1960s, she married American playwright Ferdinand Reyher, but this marriage was also challenging due to Reyher's health problems and financial difficulties. In her later years, Eileen gradually withdrew from public view, living a reclusive life while focusing on academic research and literary creation. She completed academic works such as 'The Dream of the Red Chamber' and continued writing short stories. In September 1995, Eileen Chang died alone in her Los Angeles apartment, only discovered several days later. Although her later years were impoverished, she maintained an independent spiritual world and had a profound impact on modern Chinese literature.

appraisal.zh: 张爱玲被视为中国现代文学史上最具才华的女作家之一，以细腻的心理描写和对都市生活的深刻洞察著称，其文字简洁而富张力，融古典韵味与现代主义技巧，成为连接传统与现代、东方与西方的文学桥梁，并在流行文化中化作民国上海的文化符号。另一种看法认为，她的作品多囿于个人情感与男女关系，少涉宏大历史与社会变革，与胡兰成的关系亦受非议，后期作品与英文创作未及中文之作的高度。
appraisal.en: Eileen Chang is regarded as one of the most gifted women writers of modern Chinese literature, known for delicate psychological portraiture and deep insight into urban life; her concise, tense prose blends classical resonance with modernist technique, making her a bridge between tradition and modernity, East and West, and a cultural symbol of Republican-era Shanghai. Another view holds that her fiction dwells on personal emotions and relations between men and women rather than grand history and social change, that her relationship with Hu Lancheng drew criticism, and that her later and English-language works fell short of her Chinese ones.

supporter.zh: 张爱玲被誉为中国现代文学史上最具才华的女作家之一，她的作品以细腻入微的心理描写和对都市生活的深刻洞察而著称。她打破了传统女性文学的局限，以独特的女性视角审视男女关系、婚姻制度和家庭伦理，为现代文学注入了新的活力。她的文字简洁而富有张力，意象丰富，被誉为'民国世界的临水照花人'。张爱玲的作品跨越时代和文化界限，至今仍被广泛阅读和研究，成为中国现代文学的经典。
supporter.en: Eileen Chang is regarded as one of the most talented female writers in the history of modern Chinese literature. Her works are known for their delicate psychological descriptions and profound insights into urban life. She broke through the limitations of traditional women's literature, examining relationships, marriage systems, and family ethics from a unique female perspective, injecting new vitality into modern literature. Her writing is concise yet powerful, rich in imagery, and has been described as 'the flower by the water reflecting the world of the Republic.' Her works transcend time and cultural boundaries and are still widely read and studied today, becoming classics of modern Chinese literature.

critic.zh: 批评者认为张爱玲的作品过于关注个人情感和男女关系，缺乏对时代和社会的宏大关怀。她的小说多描写都市男女的悲欢离合，较少涉及重大历史事件和社会变革。此外，她与胡兰成的感情生活也备受争议，被批评为缺乏政治立场和民族气节。一些评论家还指出，张爱玲后期作品质量有所下降，英文创作未能达到中文作品的高度，反映了她在异国文化中的适应困境。
critic.en: Critics argue that Eileen Chang's works focus too much on personal emotions and relationships, lacking grand concern for the era and society. Her novels mostly depict the joys and sorrows of urban men and women, with little involvement in major historical events and social changes. Additionally, her romantic relationship with Hu Lancheng has been controversial, criticized for lacking political stance and national integrity. Some commentators also note that the quality of her later works declined, and her English creations did not reach the height of her Chinese works, reflecting her difficulties adapting to a foreign culture.

objective.zh: 从历史和文化视角看，张爱玲被视为连接传统与现代、东方与西方的重要文学桥梁。她的作品既保留了中国古典文学的韵味，又融入了西方现代主义的技巧，形成了独特的'张爱玲式'文风。在流行文化中，她已成为一个文化符号，代表着民国时期的上海都市文化。她的作品被多次改编为电影、电视剧，影响了几代读者和观众。张爱玲的人生轨迹也反映了20世纪中国知识分子的命运变迁，从上海到香港再到美国，她的选择与经历折射出大时代下个人的挣扎与坚持。
objective.en: From a historical and cultural perspective, Eileen Chang is regarded as an important literary bridge connecting tradition and modernity, East and West. Her works preserve the charm of classical Chinese literature while incorporating techniques of Western modernism, forming a unique 'Eileen Chang-style' writing style. In popular culture, she has become a cultural symbol representing the urban culture of Shanghai during the Republican era. Her works have been adapted into films and television series multiple times, influencing generations of readers and audiences. Eileen Chang's life trajectory also reflects the changing fate of Chinese intellectuals in the 20th century, from Shanghai to Hong Kong to the United States; her choices and experiences reflect the struggles and persistence of individuals in a great era.

self.zh: 生命是一袭华美的袍，爬满了蚤子。
self.en: Life is a gorgeous robe crawling with fleas.
